blocks.title: How to Build a Philosophical Argument
items: State the **question** precisely: *Is it ever right to break a promise?*
Offer a **thesis**: *Yes, when keeping it would cause serious harm.*
List your **premises**: each must be **plausible** and **relevant**.
Check the **inference**: does the conclusion **follow from** the premises?
Anticipate the **strongest objection** and **reply** to it.
Revise: **cut** every sentence that does not **serve** the thesis.
blocks.note: A valid argument can still be unsound if a premise is false.

items.q: A premise should be plausible and relevant.
A valid argument always has true premises.

blocks.body: Um argumento sólido é **válido** (a conclusão decorre) e tem **premissas verdadeiras** (*sound*). Marcadores: **given that, since** (premissa); **hence, therefore** (conclusão).
*Valid* (forma) ≠ *true* (conteúdo): um argumento válido pode ter conclusão falsa.

items.s: Each premise must be plausible and ___. (relevant)
Does the conclusion ___ from the premises? (follow)
___, breaking a promise can be right. (therefore)
One might ___ that it erodes trust. (object)

body: **Follow from** — decorrer de
**Make a case for** — defender
**Stand to reason** — ser lógico
**Beg the question** — pressupor a conclusão
**Draw a conclusion** — tirar uma conclusão
**Hold water** — ser consistente
**Take it for granted** — dar como certo
**Leave room for doubt** — deixar margem a dúvida
**Prove one’s point** — provar o que diz
**On the contrary** — pelo contrário
**Does your conclusion follow from the premises?** — Sua conclusão decorre das premissas?
**One might object that exceptions erode trust.** — Poderiam objetar que exceções corroem a confiança.
**I think so, given that promises create trust.** — Acho que sim, dado que promessas criam confiança.

prompts.model: Given that promises create trust, we should keep them.
Therefore, breaking a promise can be justified.
One might object that exceptions erode trust.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence argument on a question of your choice, with thesis, two premises, an objection and a reply.
blocks.model: Is it ever right to lie? I will argue that it is, when the truth would cause serious harm. Given that honesty serves human wellbeing, lying is wrong by default. But since harm also damages wellbeing, there are exceptions. One might object that exceptions are easily abused. However, clear limits answer this worry.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
